Class ShortSoundPlayer

java.lang.Object
outpututils.ShortSoundPlayer
public class ShortSoundPlayer extends Object
Plays short sound effects from .wav, .aiff, or .au files.

Playback uses Clip, which loads the entire file into memory, so this class is intended for short sounds rather than long music tracks. MP3 is not supported. Audio goes directly to the operating system's audio output, so it works regardless of which terminal the program runs in (over SSH, the sound plays on the remote machine).

All playback methods block the calling thread until playback finishes. Run them on a separate thread if you need other work to continue (for example, in a GUI application). playAsync is one of the non-blocking methods which uses a background thread to play sound while the program executes.

Example: 

ShortSoundPlayer click = new ShortSoundPlayer("sounds/click.wav");
click.soundOutput();     // play the full clip
click.soundOutput(500);  // play at most the first 500 ms

  • Constructor Details

    • ShortSoundPlayer

      public ShortSoundPlayer(String soundFilePath) throws IllegalArgumentException
      Creates a player for the given sound file.

      The path is validated by file extension only. The file is not opened and its existence is not checked until one of the soundOutput methods is called.

      Parameters:
      soundFilePath - the path to the sound file; must end in .wav, .aiff, or .au (case-insensitive)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if soundFilePath is null or contains no ., or if the . is the last character of the path, or the extension is not one of the supported types

  • Method Details

    • soundOutput

      public void soundOutput()
      Plays the entire sound clip, then returns.

      This method blocks the calling thread for the full length of the clip. Playback errors (missing file, unsupported audio format, no available audio device) are not thrown; the stack trace is printed to standard error and the method returns normally. If the thread is interrupted while waiting, the stack trace is printed and playback is cut off when the clip is closed.

    • soundOutput

      public void soundOutput(int milliseconds) throws IllegalArgumentException
      Plays the sound clip for at most the given number of milliseconds, then stops it and returns.

      If milliseconds is longer than the clip, the whole clip is played and the method returns when it ends. This method blocks the calling thread while the sound plays.

      Playback errors (missing file, unsupported audio format, no available audio device) are not thrown; the stack trace is printed to standard error and the method returns normally. If the calling thread is interrupted while waiting, its interrupt flag is restored and the clip is not explicitly stopped or closed by this method.

      Parameters:
      milliseconds - the maximum playback time in milliseconds; must be zero or greater
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if milliseconds is negative

    • playAsync

      public void playAsync()
      Plays the entire sound clip without blocking the calling thread.

      This method returns as soon as playback has started. The audio is played by Java Sound's own background thread, and the clip closes itself automatically when playback stops, so the caller does not need to wait or clean up.

      Each call opens a new Clip and rereads the file from disk, so calling this method repeatedly plays overlapping copies of the sound at the same time.

      Errors that occur while setting up playback (missing file, unsupported audio format, no available audio device) are not thrown; the stack trace is printed to standard error and the method returns without playing anything. Errors that occur after playback has started are not reported.

      Playback may be cut off if the program exits before the sound finishes.
